title: Enterprise SDK Request Triage — Stakeholder Mapping & Lifecycle
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a repeatable triage and lifecycle for enterprise SDK and client-library requests that maps stakeholders, prioritization signals, and handoff steps. Focus areas: language coverage gaps, auth patterns (SSO/SAML/OAuth/KMS), streaming ergonomics (resume, backpressure, reconnect), and observability hooks. Output: a stakeholder map, a scoring rubric, and a compact intake-to-delivery lifecycle that PMs and Solutions Engineering can run for high-touch enterprise customers.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a 4-lane intake (Language Support, Auth/Identity, Streaming Ergonomics, Monitoring/Telemetry) with a shared scoring rubric that weights ARR, regulatory constraints, onboarding velocity, and engineering cost. Assign a concierge PM for requests scoring >= 60 and an eng owner for feasibility runway. Provide templated acceptance criteria and SDK API compatibility checklist for handoff to Engineering.
triage_score: manual scoring template applied; current sample score = 72
acceptance_criteria: Stakeholder map created listing: Customer Owner, SE contact, Target Product/Platform team, Eng owner
Scoring rubric documented with signal weights and examples
Two sample enterprise requests triaged end-to-end (one language add, one auth flow) with timeline estimates
Handoff docs and GitHub template created for ENG and Design
Playbook published in Confluence and announced to PM + SE rotation
notes: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after weekly Enterprise Intake review. Initial backlog includes 18 pending SDK requests from AE/SE intake form.

2026-03-03: Rapid survey of top 10 customers yielded: 6 requests for additional language bindings (Go, PHP), 4 requests for SAML/OIDC SSO patterns in SDK, 3 requests for robust streaming reconnect/resume semantics.

2026-03-04: Eng triage with Runtime team (ENG-20421) — highlighted risk: streaming resume requires KV-cache and session token pinning work; estimate 3 sprints unless scoped to client-side buffering pattern.
2026-03-06: PM sync with Legal & Security — SAML flows may require security review and policy for token lifetimes. Marked security_review_required = true.

2026-03-08: Drafted scoring rubric: ARR weight 30, Regulated customer weight 25, Onboarding velocity 20, Cross-product impact 15, Implementation complexity penalty -10. Applied to 2 pilot requests to validate thresholds.
2026-03-10: Decided on concierge threshold: score >= 60 -> dedicated PM+SE + SLA for 6-week delivery window. Lower-scored items go into self-serve roadmap with SDK contributions backlog.
2026-03-10: Links to artifacts added (see links). Next steps: run two-week pilot with SE rotation, confirm engineering capacity, create GH intake template and Confluence playbook.

Trade-offs noted: Prioritizing languages (Go, PHP) increases maintenance matrix; recommend initial strategy of providing generated bindings + reference idiomatic examples rather than full long-term maintained SDKs for lower-score requests.
